newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Forty pct of HK see Tung outdoing Patten-poll.
newsitem.headline: Forty pct of HK see Tung outdoing Patten-poll.

text.p: A significant percent of Hong Kong people expect the territory's leader-designate Tung Chee-hwa to outperform his predecessor, British colonial Governor Chris Patten, a survey showed on Thursday.
About 40.2 percent of the 1,301 respondents in a University of Hong Kong poll said they expected Tung to do a better job than Patten, while only 9.4 percent said the opposite.
A total 15.3 percent said they believed Tung's performance would be on par with Patten's. The rest did not have an opinion.

In the Wednesday survey conducted after Tung was picked to govern the territory upon its return to Chinese rule, 12.2 percent of respondents said his selection as the future leader improved their confidence in Hong Kong's future.
About 3.8 percent said his victory in the race for the top post undermined their confidence in the territory.
But the majority, 72.9 percent, said the issue did not have an impact on confidence. The rest did not have an opinion.
Respondents gave Tung an average support ranking of 70.1 out of a total of 100, his highest score ever since the university started monitoring the masses' support for him in late August.
About 39.4 percent of respondents said they were satisfied with the procedure of the leadership selection, while 31.2 percent said they were not.
The rest did not have a strong opinion.

On Wednesday, the territory's first post-colonial leader was chosen by a Beijing-controlled caucus of 400 Hong Kong people instead of by the masses. Pro-democracy parties have condemned the selection procedure as undemocratic and unrepresentative.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China next July 1, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
